01-basics.q: A Florida shop sells a taxable item and does not know of any exemption for it. What should it do?
options: Charge no tax until the Department confirms the item is taxable
Charge tax, because sales are taxable unless specifically exempt
Ask the customer whether they want to pay tax
01-basics.why: Each sale, admission, storage or rental is taxable unless the transaction is exempt, so a dealer charges tax unless a specific exemption applies.

01-basics.q: What is the state sales tax rate on electricity?
01-basics.why: Electricity is taxed at 6.95% (2.6% under Chapter 203 plus 4.35% under Chapter 212), plus surtax.

01-basics.q: A business buys office chairs from an out-of-state website that charges no Florida tax. Which tax applies?
options: Use tax, reported by the buyer
No tax, because the seller is out of state
Sales tax, collected by the Department from the seller
01-basics.why: Use tax is due on taxable items used in Florida when sales tax was not paid at purchase.

01-basics.q: When does sales tax a dealer collects become state money?
options: At the moment it is collected
When the Department deposits the payment
01-basics.why: Collected tax becomes state funds at the time of collection; the dealer holds it as custodian.

02-registration.q: A registered business opens a second location in another Florida county. Which form fits?
options: Form DR-1A, Application for Registered Businesses to Add a New Florida Location
A new Form DR-1 is always required
No registration; just update the address online
02-registration.why: A business with an active certificate uses DR-1A for an additional location or a move to another county (DR-15N R. 10/25 and the Sales and Use Tax webpage).

02-registration.q: A sole proprietor incorporates the business. What must happen?
options: Notify the Department of a name change
Submit a new registration, because the legal entity changed
02-registration.why: A change of legal entity or ownership requires a new registration (online or DR-1).

02-registration.q: Which document must be displayed in a visible place at the business location?
02-registration.why: The DR-11 authorizes business at the address shown and must be displayed visibly.

02-registration.q: A business closes on June 10. When is its final return due?
02-registration.why: A final return and all tax due must be filed within 15 days after closing or selling the business.

03-taxable-exempt.q: Which grocery-store item is taxable under DR-46NT?
03-taxable-exempt.why: Sandwiches sold ready for immediate consumption are taxable; cereal and condiments are exempt groceries.

03-taxable-exempt.q: A church treasurer buys supplies for the church with a personal credit card and is reimbursed. The church holds a DR-14. Is the sale exempt?
options: Yes, the church holds a certificate
No, payment must come from the organization's own funds
Yes, if the treasurer shows the certificate
03-taxable-exempt.why: Payment must be made with the organization's funds; personal payment later reimbursed is taxable.

03-taxable-exempt.q: A thermometer for human use is sold at a pharmacy. How is it treated?
options: Exempt, with or without a prescription
03-taxable-exempt.why: DR-46NT lists thermometers for human use among exempt chemical compounds and test kits.

03-taxable-exempt.q: Where do exempt sales go on the DR-15?
options: They are left off the return
03-taxable-exempt.why: Exempt sales, such as sales for resale and sales to DR-14 holders, are reported in Column 2.

04-services.q: Which of these services is taxable in Florida?
04-services.why: Nonresidential interior janitorial and cleaning services are among the taxable services reported on Line A; most other services are not taxed unless the law names them.

04-services.q: Does the $5,000 surtax limit apply to a $9,000 taxable security service contract?
options: No, the limit does not apply to taxable services
Only if the customer is out of state
04-services.why: The $5,000 limit applies to items of tangible personal property, not to taxable services.

04-services.q: Where is surtax sourced for a taxable service?
options: Where the customer's headquarters is located
04-services.why: Surtax on taxable services is collected at the rate of the county where the service is provided.

05-use-tax.q: A dealer bought paper towels tax free for resale, then used them in its own restroom. What is owed?
05-use-tax.why: Items bought tax exempt for resale but used by the business owe use tax.

05-use-tax.q: A dealer in a 1% surtax county buys $5,000 of equipment in a state that charged 4%. How much more is owed to Florida?
05-use-tax.why: Florida tax and surtax at 7% is $350; less the $200 legally paid to the other state leaves $150.

05-use-tax.q: Where does a registered dealer report use tax?
05-use-tax.why: Use tax goes on Line B of the DR-15; the surtax part is also reported on Line 15(d).

06-rates-surtax.q: A Florida dealer in a 1% surtax county delivers a taxable item to a customer in a county with a 1.5% surtax. Which surtax rate applies?
06-rates-surtax.why: For goods, surtax is collected at the rate of the county where delivery is made.

06-rates-surtax.q: A single $12,000 item of tangible personal property is delivered into a 1% surtax county. What is the surtax?
06-rates-surtax.why: Surtax applies only to the first $5,000 of a single item: $5,000 × 1% = $50.

06-rates-surtax.q: Tax on a sale computes to $0.074. What is charged?
06-rates-surtax.why: Carry to the third decimal place; round up only when the third decimal is greater than 4. Here it is 4, so the tax is $0.07.

06-rates-surtax.q: A motor vehicle is sold to a buyer whose registration address is in another county. Where is surtax sourced?
options: The county of the owner's residence address in the registration or title
06-rates-surtax.why: For motor vehicles and mobile homes, surtax follows the owner's residence address listed in the registration or title.

07-certificates.q: A retailer wants to use its Annual Resale Certificate to buy a laptop for its office. Is that allowed?
options: No, it is only for items that will be resold or re-rented
Yes, if the laptop costs less than $5,000
07-certificates.why: The certificate is not for items the business will use, such as furniture, office equipment, computers or supplies.

07-certificates.q: How long must a seller keep a copy of a customer's resale certificate under Method 1?
07-certificates.why: Method 1 requires keeping paper or electronic copies of the certificates for three years.

07-certificates.q: A transaction authorization number was issued for a customer's purchase on Monday. Can the seller use it for the same customer's purchase on Friday?
options: Yes, it covers the customer for the calendar year
No, it is valid only for that one purchase
07-certificates.why: A transaction authorization number is valid for that purchase only. An annual vendor authorization number (Method 3) covers a customer for the calendar year.

07-certificates.q: When do Annual Resale Certificates expire?
07-certificates.why: Annual Resale Certificates expire on December 31 of each year.

08-filing-paying.q: A quarterly filer's January to March return is due when, and late after when?
08-filing-paying.why: Returns are due on the 1st and late after the 20th of the month following the reporting period.

08-filing-paying.q: A dealer files and pays electronically and on time with an amount due of $600. What is the collection allowance?
options: $0, because the allowance needs at least $1,200 due
08-filing-paying.why: 2.5% of the first $1,200 of the amount due: 2.5% × $600 = $15.00.

08-filing-paying.q: Which business must use the DR-15 rather than the DR-15EZ?
options: A gift shop that sells only in its own county
A hotel that rents rooms to tourists
08-filing-paying.why: Businesses that lease or rent transient accommodations are not eligible for the DR-15EZ.

08-filing-paying.q: A business paid $6,200 in sales and use tax in the state fiscal year ending June 30. What changes?
options: It must file and pay electronically starting with the January return
08-filing-paying.why: Paying $5,000 or more in the prior state fiscal year requires electronic filing and payment for the next calendar year.

08-filing-paying.q: Electronic payments must be initiated, with a confirmation number, by when?
options: 5 p.m. ET on the business day before the 20th
08-filing-paying.why: To avoid penalty and interest, start the e-payment and get a confirmation number by 5 p.m. ET on the business day before the 20th.

09-rentals.q: A tenant pays August 2025 office rent in November 2025. Is sales tax due?
options: No, the commercial rent tax was repealed October 1, 2025
Yes, 2% plus any surtax, because the rental period was before October 1, 2025
09-rentals.why: Rent for periods through September 2025 stays taxable at 2% plus surtax even if paid on or after October 1, 2025 (TIP 25A01-04).

09-rentals.q: A marina rents boat slips by the month. After October 1, 2025, how is that treated?
options: Exempt under the commercial rent repeal
Taxable at 6% plus surtax and reported on Line A
09-rentals.why: Docking and storage are taxed under a different section and were not affected by the repeal. Report them on Line A (TIP 25A01-11).

09-rentals.q: A condo is rented for a seven-month stay. Is it a transient rental?
options: No, transient rentals are six months or less
Only if the owner lives in Florida
09-rentals.why: Transient rentals are rentals of accommodations for six months or less.

09-rentals.q: Where does state sales tax on transient rentals get reported?
options: To whichever agency collects the tourist development tax
09-rentals.why: Many counties collect their local transient rental taxes directly, but state tax and surtax on transient rentals always go to the Department.

10-vehicles-boats-aircraft.q: A dealer in a 1% surtax county sells a car to a buyer whose registration address is in a 1.5% county. Which surtax rate applies?
10-vehicles-boats-aircraft.why: For motor vehicles, surtax follows the owner's residence address on the registration or title.

10-vehicles-boats-aircraft.q: A boat and trailer sold together on one invoice for $55,000 to a buyer in a 1.5% county. What is the surtax?
10-vehicles-boats-aircraft.why: Since July 1, 2024 they count as one item, so surtax applies to the first $5,000: $5,000 × 1.5% = $75 (TIP 24A01-11).

10-vehicles-boats-aircraft.q: What is the state rate on a new mobile home?
10-vehicles-boats-aircraft.why: Since July 1, 2022, retail sales of new mobile homes are taxed at 3%. Used mobile homes are taxed at 6%.

10-vehicles-boats-aircraft.q: A resident of a state with a 4% rate buys a car in Florida and files a DR-123. How much Florida tax is collected?
options: Nothing; they pay their home state
10-vehicles-boats-aircraft.why: Under the partial exemption, Florida collects tax equal to the home state's rate, and the tax collected is Florida sales tax.

11-food-restaurants.q: A bakery with tables sells three muffins on a tray. Taxable?
options: Yes, five or fewer items are presumed eaten on the premises
11-food-restaurants.why: TIP 10A01-22: bakery products sold in quantities of five or fewer are presumed sold for consumption on the premises.

11-food-restaurants.q: Concession receipts in a 7% county are $100, all taxable. What is the tax due?
A bar posts signs saying tax is included in drink prices. Which method does it use?
options: Multiply receipts by the effective rate
11-food-restaurants.why: Method 2, used when customers are told tax is included, divides receipts by the divisor (GT-800046).

11-food-restaurants.q: Is candy exempt as a grocery?
options: No, items advertised as candy are taxable
11-food-restaurants.why: DR-46NT: candy and similar items regarded and advertised as candy are taxable.

12-contractors-manufacturing.q: What is the indexed tax per ton on contractor-made asphalt for July 2026 to June 2027?
12-contractors-manufacturing.why: TIP 26A01-02 sets $1.19 per ton for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, up from $1.16.

12-contractors-manufacturing.q: A farmer shows a Florida Farm TEAM Card. How does the seller document the exempt sale?
options: Keep a copy of the card, or get an authorization number
Have the farmer sign a DR-13
12-contractors-manufacturing.why: TIP 24A01-01: keep a copy of the TEAM Card, or get a transaction or vendor authorization number.

12-contractors-manufacturing.q: How does a homeowner get the 2026 home-hardening exemption?
options: At the register by showing a homestead card
Only through a refund, up to $500
12-contractors-manufacturing.why: TIP 26A01-09: the exemption is refund-only, capped at $500 for one eligible property.

13-admissions.q: A concert ticket bought for $100 (with $6 tax) is resold for $150. What tax does the reseller remit, assuming no surtax?
13-admissions.why: TIP 17A01-13: collect tax on the higher price ($9) and credit the tax previously paid ($6).

13-admissions.q: What is the tax rate on coin-operated amusement machine receipts?
13-admissions.why: GT-800020: amusement machine charges are taxed at 4% plus any surtax.

13-admissions.q: Are Florida State Parks admissions taxable after July 1, 2025?
13-admissions.why: TIP 25A01-07: State Parks admissions, including annual passes, are exempt from July 1, 2025.

14-remote-marketplace.q: An out-of-state seller had $90,000 of taxable remote sales into Florida last year. Must it register?
options: No, the threshold is more than $100,000
Only if it has a website
14-remote-marketplace.why: A substantial number of remote sales means more than $100,000 in the previous calendar year (TIP 21A01-03).

14-remote-marketplace.q: A marketplace provider certifies it will collect on a seller's sales. What does the seller do with those sales?
options: Leave them off its return and not collect
14-remote-marketplace.why: When the provider certifies, the seller may not collect and excludes those sales from its return.

14-remote-marketplace.q: A restaurant's delivery app returns the tax it collects to the restaurant. Who remits it?
14-remote-marketplace.why: Unless the delivery network elects to collect and remit, the merchant is responsible (TIP 23A01-24).

15-holidays-exemption-periods.q: During the 2026 Hunting, Fishing, and Camping holiday, is a $220 tent exempt?
options: No, tents are limited to $200 or less
15-holidays-exemption-periods.why: TIP 26A01-06 lists tents at a sales price of $200 or less.

15-holidays-exemption-periods.q: Can a dealer opt out of the annual Back-to-School holiday?
15-holidays-exemption-periods.why: TIP 26A01-11: dealers cannot opt out of the Back-to-School holiday.

15-holidays-exemption-periods.q: Is a portable generator rated at 8,000 running watts taxable today?
options: No, it has been always exempt since August 1, 2025
15-holidays-exemption-periods.why: TIP 25A01-05 made portable generators of 10,000 running watts or less always exempt from August 1, 2025.

16-records-audits.q: How long must records be kept?
options: At least three years from when the return was filed or due, whichever is later
16-records-audits.why: Records must be kept at least three years from the date the return was filed or required to be filed, whichever is later.

options: A Notice of Intent to Audit Books and Records (DR-840)
16-records-audits.why: GT-800022: the DR-840 starts the 60-day notice period.

16-records-audits.q: How long does a taxpayer have to file a formal protest after a Notice of Proposed Assessment?
16-records-audits.why: 60 days for an informal protest; 120 days for a formal protest (GT-800022).

17-penalties-interest-refunds.q: A return with $200 of tax due is filed late. What is the penalty?
17-penalties-interest-refunds.why: The penalty is 10% of the amount due, with a $50 minimum.

17-penalties-interest-refunds.q: $2,000 of tax is paid 21 days late at a daily factor of 0.000301370. What is the interest?
How long does a dealer have to claim a sales tax refund?
options: Three years from the date the tax was paid
17-penalties-interest-refunds.why: The claim must be received within three years of the date the tax was paid (refunds page).

options: Taxpayers the Department has not contacted about the liability
17-penalties-interest-refunds.why: Eligibility requires that the Department has not previously contacted the taxpayer about the liability.

18-capstone.q: In the capstone, why is only $5,000 of the $8,000 sculpture subject to surtax?
options: The buyer is out of state
18-capstone.why: Surtax applies only to the first $5,000 of a single item of tangible personal property.

18-capstone.q: Why is Harbor Light's collection allowance $30 and not 2.5% of $2,991?
options: The allowance is 2.5% of only the first $1,200, so it can't exceed $30

18-capstone.q: Which capstone items go on Line B?
options: The out-of-state shelving and the inventory used in the office
18-capstone.why: Untaxed out-of-state purchases and resale inventory used by the business owe use tax, reported on Line B.

08a-efile-pay.q: A dealer paid $4,000 in sales and use tax last state fiscal year and files one return for a single location. Must it file electronically?
options: No, but it may choose to
Yes, every dealer must since December 1, 2025
08a-efile-pay.why: Electronic filing is required after a fiscal year with $5,000 or more paid, or for consolidated filers. Others may file electronically voluntarily, and the new system did not change who must.

08a-efile-pay.q: A guest user's Business Partner Number is 0001234567. How should it be entered?
options: It can't be used; guests must enroll first
08a-efile-pay.why: TIP 25A01-19: when entering the Business Partner Number, do not include leading zeros.

08a-efile-pay.q: Per DR-659, what makes an electronic payment on time?
options: Completing it and receiving the confirmation number by 5 p.m. ET on the DR-659 date
Choosing a debit date on or before the 20th
Starting it any time before midnight on the 20th
08a-efile-pay.why: DR-659: complete the payment and receive a confirmation number by 5 p.m. ET on the listed date, usually the business day before the 20th.

08a-efile-pay.q: A dealer paid by credit card and then noticed the amount was wrong. Can the payment be canceled online?
options: No, card payments cannot be canceled
Yes, until 5 p.m. ET that day
Yes, if they log in as a guest
08a-efile-pay.why: The FAQ says credit card payments cannot be canceled. Only ACH debits can be, before 5 p.m. ET on the day they were submitted.

08a-efile-pay.q: A business files one consolidated return for 12 locations. In eFile and Pay, how is it built?
options: A DR-7 for each location is saved, then the DR-15CON is reviewed and submitted
One DR-15 with all locations' sales added together
08a-efile-pay.why: The consolidated guide: open a DR-7 for each Location ID, save each one, then use Review Consolidated Return to submit the DR-15CON.

08a-efile-pay.q: The bank keeps rejecting a dealer's ACH debit because of a debit block. What fixes it?
options: Give the bank the Department's sales and use tax company ID, 7596001874
08a-efile-pay.why: GT-800012 lists the company identifiers to give the bank. For sales and use tax it is 7596001874.
